security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's ssp CSR access check in VU-mode evaluates the raw senvcfg.SSE backing-store bit instead of the effective value derived through the menvcfg.SSE→henvcfg.SSE→senvcfg.SSE read-only-zero cascade. Specifically, when menvcfg.SSE=0 forces both henvcfg.SSE and senvcfg.SSE to read-only zero, QEMU may fail to enforce this cascade on the write path (allowing a stale senvcfg.SSE=1 to persist in backing storage) or on the access-check path (reading the stale backing bit instead of the masked effective zero), causing ssp to be accessible when the spec mandates a virtual-instruction exception.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: read-only zero cascade not enforced on subordinate CSR fields; write-side WARL masking decoupled from read-side zero-return; ssp access check reads raw backing field instead of effective masked field; menvcfg.SSE clear does not force-clear or write-protect henvcfg.SSE/senvcfg.SSE backing storage
security_spec.summary: Zicfiss ssp CSR VU-mode access now depends solely on effective senvcfg.SSE (via menvcfg→henvcfg→senvcfg read-only-zero cascade); QEMU must ensure both read masking and write blocking propagate through the full cascade, or VU-mode guests gain unauthorized shadow-stack pointer access
